name: manifest-dev
description: Manifest-driven development: /figure-out reaches shared understanding, /define writes Deliverables with Acceptance Criteria and Global Invariants, and /do implements them. Each gate is one text — a title, a body, and an optional why — carrying a required kind (judgment or deterministic, never inferred) as its only structured metadata; execution policy is selected at /do launch as per-gate (independent default), consolidated, or self, with an optional verifier model for independent modes. Every mode keeps a provenance-rich gate ledger and the run never downgrades itself. Re-verification follows each gate's declared kind: command-backed gates re-run in full, while judgment gates take one full look and then judge only prior findings' repairs and the changed delta, with --exhaustive-verification restoring full re-sampling. A default-on execution log preserves deviations and dead-end memory; --no-log opts out. For unattended runs, use a host-native goal-setting backstop whose completion contract requires fresh PASS evidence for every gate under the selected mode. /auto chains the full flow, and /figure-out-team extends deliberation to multi-party Slack sessions. /ticket-up authors convention-compliant Tickets from a Manifest, direct work, independently managed questions, or source-linked follow-ups; one Manifest becomes one coherent Shaped Ticket by default, with Deliverable splitting reserved for explicit delegation. Follow-up Auto preserves source authority for unattended or nested authoring, while a person at the ticket-up boundary may freshly grant Auto after the new Ticket independently qualifies. /next-ticket claims and presents the ready Ticket whose delay would lose the most project value for the human-plus-AI session, using current executor time rather than traditional feature-size estimates. /run-ticket receives one exact Ticket, recovers its stable branch and pull request, invokes /auto, completes required landing, and records DONE or ESCALATED on that Ticket. /sweep-tickets recovers first or starts one eligible Auto Ticket by the same delay-loss objective per scheduled invocation. Stores use the project's shared tracker, GitHub Issues out of the box, or files where cross-checkout claiming is not needed. /init-context sets a repository up with the surfaces the workflow reads from — project-owned ADR conventions, a glossary, and the context-file wiring that keeps sessions using them — seeding them from the project's own history where there is any.
